original_test_intent: Validate that supported GPUs can enter and leave MIG mode, expose the approved profile catalogue when enabled, and return to the original mode/partition state without losing managed workloads.
original_method: Map GPU UUID/BDF/SKU and MIG capability; inventory baseline mode, GPU/compute instances and clients; drain workloads and obtain critical approval; enable intended devices, handle required reset/reboot only as approved, verify mode and profile catalogue; disable and verify absence; restore original mode and recreate exact baseline instances if required; confirm clients and health.
manual_activity: GPU/cluster owner authorizes the disruptive maintenance window, workload eviction and exact restore plan; agent may perform one bounded transition transaction afterward.
required_inputs: Baseline MIG mode and complete GI/CI placement/profile map
Approved profile catalogue and expected mode behavior
Reset/reboot/OOB recovery and exact recreation plan
safety_requirements: Never toggle MIG with active unapproved clients
Treat existing GI/CI state as recoverable configuration data
Do not reset/reboot or destroy instances without explicit approval
Target explicit UUIDs and stop on first transition/health anomaly
No automatic retry; restore baseline under owner control
agent_execution_scope: Validate capability, baseline, drain and approval
Restore mode and exact prior instance topology as authorized
Collect health and report without DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Own scheduler, reset/reboot and failed-restore recovery

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: Profile/mode queries are useful evidence but do not exercise source-required -mig 1 and -mig 0 actions.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: After critical approval, toggle only explicit GPU UUID targets, verify mode plus `mig -lgip`, and restore the captured per-GPU mode/GI/CI topology.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Enable, profile-list, disable and post-disable checks are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a transactional MIG state manifest covering mode, GI/CI profiles, placement and clients before and after each transition.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds capability selection, workload coordination and exact reconstruction.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Preserves actual management transitions instead of accepting inventory-only evidence.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Mode changes can require GPU reset/reboot and invalidate all instances/contexts; restoration may be scheduler-dependent.

project_override_considerations: Cluster policy governs which GPUs may enter MIG mode and the authoritative profile catalogue and instance placement.
expected_evidence: Exact transition/profile commands, outputs, exits and timestamps
Restored instance topology, clients and health

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Procedure and Criteria consistently require MIG enable/disable behavior; DeepSeek omission is not a Master contradiction.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The test is provisionable under a controlled maintenance transaction; absent approvals are tracked readiness inputs.

review_improvement: Protects pre-existing MIG partitions and workloads while retaining both destructive source transitions.
independent_technical_reasoning: MIG mode is not a harmless flag: switching it can require a GPU reset and removes the device topology on which GI/CI clients depend. Therefore a profile listing cannot substitute for the test, and safe execution depends on a complete reconstructable baseline plus scheduler-aware drain and recovery.
